q: What do you call an equivalent load applied to a single point?
n: A point (concentrated) load is idealized as acting at one point. A uniformly distributed load spreads over a length or area.
ref: NSCP 2015 (NSCP C101-15), Sec. 204 - Dead Loads and load definitions

q: Per NSCP Table 204-2, what is the dead load of ceramic or quarry tile (20 mm) on a 25 mm mortar bed?
n: Ceramic or quarry tile 20 mm thick on a 25 mm mortar bed carries a dead load of 1.10 kPa.
ref: NSCP 2015 (NSCP C101-15), Table 204-2 Minimum Design Dead Loads

q: Per NSCP Table 204-2, what is the dead load of gypsum board per mm of thickness?
n: Gypsum board is 0.008 kPa per mm of thickness.
ref: NSCP 2015 (NSCP C101-15), Table 204-2 Minimum Design Dead Loads

q: Using NSCP Table 204-2, what is the dead load of 12 mm thick gypsum board?
ref: NSCP 2015 (NSCP C101-15), Table 204-2 Minimum Design Dead Loads

q: Per NSCP Table 204-2, what is the dead load of a suspended steel channel ceiling system?
n: Suspended steel channel system is 0.10 kPa in the ceilings group of Table 204-2.
ref: NSCP 2015 (NSCP C101-15), Table 204-2 Minimum Design Dead Loads

q: Per NSCP Table 204-2, what is the dead load of a wood furring suspension system?
n: Wood furring suspension system is 0.12 kPa in the ceilings group of Table 204-2.
ref: NSCP 2015 (NSCP C101-15), Table 204-2 Minimum Design Dead Loads

q: Per NSCP Table 204-2, what is the dead load of a wood-joist floor (no plaster) using 50 × 150 mm joists at 300 mm spacing?
n: The wood-joist floor rows give 0.30 kPa for 50 × 150 joists at 300 mm o.c. The load drops to 0.25 kPa at 400 and 600 mm spacing, so read the spacing carefully.
ref: NSCP 2015 (NSCP C101-15), Table 204-2 Minimum Design Dead Loads

q: For a beam analyzed as simply supported, how is the effective span generally determined (NSCP / ACI 318 practice)?
o: Always the center-to-center distance of the supports
Always the clear span between faces of supports
The clear span minus the depth of the member
Clear span plus the depth of the member, but not more than the center-to-center distance of supports
n: The effective span is the clear span plus the depth of the member, but it need not exceed the center-to-center distance between supports.
ref: NSCP 2015 (NSCP C101-15), Sec. 408 / ACI 318 - span length of members not built integrally with supports
